elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 9.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor"; the conforming edit to 2.1 removes the former "or termination rights" bar and makes the take-or-pay commitment "subject to Section 9.4", so no retained sentence contradicts the right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 9.4 requires "thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — exactly the 30-day ceiling, in writing.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 9.4: "Vendor shall refund, on a pro rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination" — the pro rata basis is express (not merely inferred from a post-termination period) and covers Fees as defined, not just recurring Fees as in 10.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: 9.4 second sentence: "Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Sections 9.1–9.3 give Vendor only breach and insolvency exits, so no residual Vendor convenience right survives.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 9.4 sets thirty days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (more favourable to us, but literally not this element).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no operative early-termination fee or penalty is imposed on Customer's 9.4 exit, and 2.1 retains only a no-reduction restriction expressly subject to 9.4, so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 9.4 bars Vendor convenience termination during a committed term and no clause grants Vendor any convenience right elsewhere (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency only), which is at least as restrictive as term-end-only.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor holds no convenience termination right after 9.4, so no Vendor notice period is triggered.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Duplicate-level check for completeness: covered by 9.4's express prohibition on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: 9.4 supplies the Customer convenience right over both the Agreement and any Order Form, a 30-day written notice period, an express pro rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and a flat prohibition on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

Minimality holds: the insertion tracks the model language without the surplus "in whole or in part", and adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, or extra remedy. The only other edit is the narrowly conforming change to 2.1, which deletes the words that would otherwise contradict the new right and retains the Customer-adverse-but-existing "without reduction rights" restriction; the "subject to Section 9.4" pointer is a conforming cross-reference rather than a duplicated operative term.

Intent is preserved: 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 termination rights and the 10.2 wind-down/refund mechanics survive intact and are not contradicted (9.4's broader pro rata refund applies to convenience exits; 10.2 continues to apply to breach-driven refunds), and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created — Section 9.4 exists as rendered.
Fallback level is not complete (30-day notice sits outside the 60–90 day band), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is fully met; a redline needs only one complete level.

No repair required. If Vendor pushes back, the only defensible retreat is to move 9.4 notice to 60 days and, if Vendor insists on any exit, cap it at term-end with 90 days' notice — do not accept reinstatement of "or termination rights" in 2.1.
